verdict.rationale: Sardine's own marketing pages say its AI agents auto-clear low-risk or obvious false-positive sanctions matches and route higher-risk matches to analysts for review, which covers the escalate-to-human half of the story. The evidence never documents a policy that limits what the agents may resolve automatically: configurable rules and fuzzy-match thresholds exist, but they are not shown to govern agent auto-clearing. missing for 10: documented policy controls over the scope of automatic agent remediation, explicit handling of ambiguous findings, first-party technical docs (beyond marketing pages), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a ai-native, I can limit automatic remediation by policy and escalate ambiguous or high-risk findings to a human

citations.quote: AI agents clear obvious false positives, perform supporting research, and route higher-risk matches for analyst review.
Auto-clear low-risk matches and escalate real exposure with explainable scores.
